Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a workout into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme workout and deliver a live timeline: Erg Session — four rowers, two machines for 4 rowers, 2 ergs, 3 pieces
Resource limits: two ergs, four rowers, one coach, one rower on the coached drill at a time.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Erg Session — four rowers, two machines

Two ergs in the bay and four of us, so we row in pairs and the pair that is off the machines is the pair that is resting. A and B are the first pair, C and D the second. Nobody sits on a machine they are not rowing.

Warm-up
A and B warm up first: 10 minutes, rate 18, light pressure, half slide to full slide.
C and D come in ten minutes later and take the machines for their own 10 minute warm-up.

The pieces
Three pieces, four minutes each, rate 26 to 28, target split on the monitor.
A and B take the first piece as soon as C and D are off the machines.
C and D take the first piece straight off the back of A and B's first piece.
A and B start their second piece four minutes after their first one ends.
C and D take the second piece as soon as A and B are off.
A and B start their third piece four minutes after their second one ends.
C and D take the third piece as soon as A and B are off.

Technique drill
Three minutes each, one at a time, coach on the machine with you: pause at the finish, pause at half slide, then build. A goes first once C and D are off the last piece, then B, then C, then D.

Cooldown
Ten minutes on the floor together once the last drill is done: legs up the wall, hips, lats, then a cup of tea.

Coach
Brief the crew on the boards before anyone gets on: 5 minutes.
Call splits from the first piece: 20 minutes on the clock, watch the catch not the monitor.
Run the drills: 12 minutes, one rower at a time, straight through.
Debrief after the cooldown: 10 minutes, what the splits said and what Saturday looks like.

Note
The rests are not steps for the first pair: they are the gap between one piece ending and the next one starting, because the machines are handed over in that gap and the second pair is using them. The second pair's rests are the first pair's pieces. That is the whole design of the session.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

The Erg Session is a workout being planned for four rowers, utilizing two rowing machines. The session is designed to be completed as early as the work allows, with no specific finishing time given. The constraints include having only two rowing machines available, four rowers participating, one coach available to guide the rowers through drills one at a time, and the need to manage the rowers' time on and off the machines efficiently.

```json
{
  "summary": "An Erg Session workout for four rowers using two rowing machines, to be completed as early as possible, constrained by two ergs, four rowers, and one coach available for individual drills.",
  "servesOrScale": "4 rowers",
  "deadline": "as early as possible",
  "constraints": ["2 rowing machines", "4 rowers", "1 coach"]
}
```

The target data model for the Rhylthyme program consists of parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, where each step has a duration and a **startTrigger** that determines when it begins. The duration of a step can be `fixed`, `variable`, or `indefinite`. The `startTrigger` can reference other steps or the program start time, allowing for complex dependencies between steps. `stepId`s must be unique across the entire program, not just within a track. Every `task` used by a step must have a corresponding `resourceConstraints` entry, which defines the maximum number of steps that can use that task concurrently. Repeated work is handled using the `replicates` feature, which allows a step to be repeated multiple times with different instances, and downstream steps can be triggered based on the completion of individual instances or all instances.

For the Erg Session workout, the expected resource constraints are:
- `erg`: 2 (since there are two rowing machines available)
- `drill`: 1 (since the coach can only work with one rower at a time)
- `coaching`: 1 (implicitly, as there is one coach)
- `rower`: 4 (since there are four rowers participating)

However, upon closer inspection, it seems that "rower" isn't a task that needs to be constrained in the same way as "erg" or "drill" because the limitation is more about the coordination of the rowers rather than the rowers being a resource. Thus, the primary constraints are on the ergs and the coaching/drill.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "Tracks are sequential; steps have one duration kind; triggers link steps; stepIds are global; every task needs a resourceConstraint; repeated work is handled with replicates.",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "erg", "maxConcurrent": 2 },
    { "task": "drill", "maxConcurrent": 1 }
  ],
  "actors": 4
}
```

List every timed activity you would have to perform, in the order the text gives it, with:

- a short kebab-case `stepId` and a human `name`;
- `task`: the resource it occupies while it runs — the oven, a burner, the thermocycler, the PA, the bench, your own hands. Use the same name every time for the same resource;
- how long it takes: exact (`fixed`), a range (`variable`), or "until I decide" (`indefinite`);
- `sourceSpan`: the exact words in the text you took it from, as `{"quote": "...", "occurrence": n}`, where n says which occurrence of those words you mean (1 for the first). Quote the text verbatim — do not paraphrase it;
- `inferred`: `true` for a step the text never states but the work needs anyway (preheating, thawing, resting, cooling, labelling, sound-check), with `"sourceSpan": null`. Keep these few and obvious.

Split anything the text bundles into one sentence when the parts occupy different resources or different stretches of time ("brown the meat, then simmer for 40 minutes" is two activities). Do not decide yet which activities can overlap, which track they belong to, or what waits for what.

Reply with the step list as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:
